_comment: WeChat archive and ingest (2026-10-29, Albert). Two halves: scripts/wechat_archive.py runs on Albert's Mac (launchd, early morning), reads WeChat through the macOS Accessibility API and inserts every message not yet recorded into the private Notion database below; scripts/wechat_pull.py runs anywhere (cloud /daily-ingest included) and only reads that database. Method and setup: methods/wechat-archive.md. Every tunable lives here, never in the scripts.

notion._comment: The WeChat Archive database, created 2026-10-29 as a private workspace-level page. Two internal integrations are shared with it and nothing else: the writer (Read content + Insert content, no Update) on the Mac only, and the reader (Read content only) for wechat_pull.py. Insert-only is the structural guarantee that the archiver can never edit or delete a row.
notion._heartbeat_comment: Every archiver run, including one that skips, inserts one row in this pseudo-chat with Kind=system and a JSON summary in Text. wechat_pull.py excludes it from messages and reports the newest one, so a Mac that stopped running is a finding instead of a quiet day.

archive._max_chats_comment: Chats taken from the top of WeChat's sidebar (most recent first). A chat further down had no new message since the last run unless more than this many chats were active in a day.
archive._backfill_comment: Each chat is read newest-first, tail_check_messages at a time. If the stored tail can't be found in that window, the archiver reads up to backfill_cap_messages and, failing that, writes what it read with Gap before ticked on the first row.
archive._first_run_comment: How far back a chat with no stored messages starts. Older history is not archived.
archive._idle_comment: The reader takes focus, clicks and scrolls. It starts only when the keyboard and mouse have been idle this long and never on a locked screen, and it stops between chats the moment someone touches the Mac.

schedule._comment: A Mac is usually locked at a fixed early hour, and a locked screen can't be read. So launchd fires every_minutes and the archiver runs the first time, after first_attempt, that the Mac is unlocked and idle, then not again until min_hours_between_runs after the last completed run. An attempt that isn't due or finds the Mac locked or busy exits without writing anything; a day with no completed run shows up as a stale heartbeat in the brief. Lower min_hours_between_runs to archive more than once a day.

archive._skip_comment: Exact sidebar names never opened. Add a personal chat here to keep it out of the archive.

parse._comment: Patterns are a best guess at what WeChat for Mac exposes through Accessibility, in English and Chinese UI. They are data so the first supervised run can correct them without a code change.

ingest._window_comment: Overlaps a day so a late archiver run is still read; the agent dedupes against nothing, it just summarises what arrived in the window.
